summary: Choi et al. (2025) report multi-agent debate simulations (2,500+ debates across five contentious topics) in which a GPT-4o neutral moderator evaluates proponent/opponent LLM agents and picks the most persuasive side each turn. Three anchored findings satisfy the node: (1) neutral agents significantly conform to the numerically dominant group (χ2=164.839, p<0.001), (2) neutral agents significantly conform to higher-intelligence agents even when outnumbered (χ2=142.285, p<0.001; e.g., scenario g, 2 superior proponents CR 83.17 vs scenario h, 2 inferior opponents 25.67), and (3) a single high-intelligence agent outperforms a larger lower-intelligence group (CR 74.33 vs 63.53–72.11 for equivalent-intelligence majorities; stated explicitly in the paper). These are empirical claims from the supplied workspace file, each anchored to specific PDF page markers (pages 6 and 7 primarily).
unresolved: I did not extract Choi et al.'s qualitative 'spiral of silence' examples as a separate finding; they are documented on PDF PAGE 8 and 17, but they are less central to the majority/intelligence conformity conditions that the node asks for.
